messages:
alex: Heads up — my Go HTTP client started returning 401s talking to api.redwood.example even though curl with the same API key works. I read the key from /run/secrets and set Authorization: Basic <base64>. Any quick ideas?

mari: paste your read+header code and the exact curl you ran.

alex: minimal snippet:

```
data, _ := os.ReadFile("/run/secrets/redwood_key")
key := string(data)
enc := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(key))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+enc)
```

curl I tested:

```
export API_KEY=$(cat /run/secrets/redwood_key)
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo $API_KEY | base64)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

samir: most likely culprit: trailing newline in the secret file. cat/echo often include a final \n, os.ReadFile preserves it, so base64 differs. Use hexdump to check for 0a.

mari: quick commands to inspect:
- `xxd -g 1 -u /run/secrets/redwood_key | head` (look for 0A at end)
- `hexdump -C /run/secrets/redwood_key | head`
- compare encodings: `echo -n "${KEY}" | base64` vs `echo "${KEY}" | base64`

samir: safe Go patterns:

```
raw, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
raw = bytes.TrimRight(raw, []byte("\r\n")) // strip CR/LF only
enc := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(raw)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+enc)
```

or if you already have a string:

```
key = strings.TrimRight(key, "\r\n")
```

but avoid TrimSpace since it removes spaces that might be part of the key.

alex: thanks — that was it. File had a trailing newline from the build step. TrimRight fixed the 401. I pushed a tiny fix and added a test that writes the secret with a trailing \n and verifies header bytes.

mari: also watch for BOM (UTF-8 EF BB BF) and CRLF (\r\n) on secrets coming from Windows. Quick check for BOM: `head -c 3 file | xxd`.

devex-bot: doc: devex/faq#auth-files — common issues: trailing newlines, BOMs, echo vs printf, CI runners adding \n.
